questions.exp: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with the help of Chanakya. It became one of the largest empires in ancient India.

questions.q: The Indus Valley Civilization was discovered in which year?
questions.exp: The Indus Valley Civilization was discovered in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni at Harappa and R.D. Banerji at Mohenjo-daro.
The Arthashastra was written by Chanakya (Kautilya), adviser to Chandragupta Maurya. It is a treatise on statecraft and economic policy.

questions.q: The Battle of Kalinga was fought in which year?
questions.exp: The Battle of Kalinga was fought in 261 BCE. After witnessing its bloodshed, Emperor Ashoka converted to Buddhism and adopted a policy of non-violence.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler is known as 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.exp: Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya, was the most powerful Gupta emperor. His reign is called the golden age of ancient India.

questions.q: The Ajanta Caves were built during which dynasty?
questions.exp: The Ajanta Caves were primarily built during the Vakataka period (5th–6th century CE). They contain remarkable Buddhist paintings and sculptures.

questions.q: Who was the last ruler of the Maurya Empire?
questions.exp: Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Maurya Empire. He was assassinated by his general Pushyamitra Shunga around 185 BCE.

questions.q: The city of Mohenjo-daro is located in present-day which country?
questions.exp: Mohenjo-daro is located in present-day Pakistan, in the Sindh province. It was one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.q: Which ancient Indian university attracted scholars from across Asia?
questions.exp: Nalanda University (5th–12th century CE) was one of the greatest centers of learning in the ancient world, attracting students from China, Korea, Japan, and beyond.

questions.q: The Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas. How many hymns does it contain approximately?
questions.exp: The Rig Veda contains 1028 hymns organized into 10 mandalas (books). It is the oldest known Vedic text and is considered one of the oldest religious texts in the world.
